Fitted values, residuals, interpolation and updating of JDemetra+ models

Source: R/methods.R
jd3_model_methods_extra.Rd

Methods for models fitted with X13(), TRAMOSEATS(), REGARIMA() or TRAMO(). They can be applied directly on a mable.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'jd3_model'
fitted(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'jd3_model'
residuals(object, type = c("innovation", "regression"), ...)

# S3 method for class 'jd3_model'
interpolate(object, new_data = NULL, specials = NULL, ...)

# S3 method for class 'jd3_model'
refit(
  object,
  new_data,
  specials = NULL,
  policy = c("Fixed", "FreeParameters", "Complete", "Outliers_StochasticComponent",
    "Outliers", "FixedParameters", "FixedAutoRegressiveParameters", "Current"),
  period = 0,
  start = NULL,
  end = NULL,
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'jd3_model'
stream(
  object,
  new_data,
  specials = NULL,
  policy = c("Fixed", "FreeParameters", "Complete", "Outliers_StochasticComponent",
    "Outliers", "FixedParameters", "FixedAutoRegressiveParameters", "Current"),
  period = 0,
  start = NULL,
  end = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

object

A fitted jd3_model (usually a column of a mable).

...

Currently unused.

type

Residual type: "innovation" (default) or "regression".

new_data

A tsibble. For interpolate(), the data with missing values (same dates as the data of the model). For refit(), the new full data. For stream(), the new observations only.

specials

Currently unused.

policy

Refresh policy, a character string (see the functions above for the available policies; default "Fixed": the estimated parameters are kept).

period, start, end

additional parameters used to specify the span when policy = "Current" or policy = "Outliers" or policy = "Outliers_StochasticComponent" period: numeric, number of observations in a year (12, 4...), compulsory, if false or missing, re-estimation with refreshed specification won't work. When policy = "Outliers" or policy = "Outliers_StochasticComponent" start has to be specified as the date from which outliers will be re-identified end is not used, if specified it will be ignored. When policy = "Current" start and end have to be both specified and indicate the span on which additive outliers (AO) will be added. Span definition: start and end: defined as arrays of two elements: year and first period (for example, period = 12 and start=c(1980, 1) stands for January 1980)

Value

  • fitted(), residuals(): a numeric vector with one value per observation (NA where undefined). Called on a mable, a tibble with the index and the .fitted or .resid column.

  • interpolate(): new_data with the missing values filled in.

  • refit(), stream(): a jd3_model fitted on the new data. Called on a mable, a mable.

Details

  • fitted() returns the one-step-ahead fitted values of the pre-adjustment model, on the scale of the series. Together with residuals(), it makes augment() and accuracy() work.

  • residuals() returns the innovation residuals of the pre-adjustment model (type = "innovation") or the linearized series the ARIMA part is applied to (type = "regression"). Dates for which a residual is not defined (e.g. lost to differencing) are NA.

  • interpolate() replaces the missing values of the series by the estimates of the model. new_data must cover the same dates as the data used to fit the model.

  • refit() applies the model to new data, using a JDemetra+ refresh policy (see rjd3x13::x13_refresh() and rjd3tramoseats::tramoseats_refresh()): the specification is refreshed from the estimated model and the reference specification stored in the model (see the ref_spec argument of X13()).

  • stream() appends new observations to the data of the model and refreshes it in the same way. new_data contains the new observations only.

See also

X13(), TRAMOSEATS(), forecast.jd3_model(), jd3_model_methods

Examples

y  <- as_tsibble(AirPassengers)
mb <- model(y, x13 = X13(value))

# Fitted values and residuals (also used by augment() and accuracy())
fitted(mb)
#> # A tsibble: 144 x 3 [1M]
#> # Key:       .model [1]
#>    .model    index .fitted
#>    <chr>     <mth>   <dbl>
#>  1 x13    1949 Jan      NA
#>  2 x13    1949 Feb      NA
#>  3 x13    1949 Mar      NA
#>  4 x13    1949 Apr      NA
#>  5 x13    1949 May      NA
#>  6 x13    1949 Jun      NA
#>  7 x13    1949 Jul      NA
#>  8 x13    1949 Aug      NA
#>  9 x13    1949 Sep      NA
#> 10 x13    1949 Oct      NA
#> # ℹ 134 more rows
residuals(mb)                         # innovation residuals
#> # A tsibble: 144 x 3 [1M]
#> # Key:       .model [1]
#>    .model    index .resid
#>    <chr>     <mth>  <dbl>
#>  1 x13    1949 Jan     NA
#>  2 x13    1949 Feb     NA
#>  3 x13    1949 Mar     NA
#>  4 x13    1949 Apr     NA
#>  5 x13    1949 May     NA
#>  6 x13    1949 Jun     NA
#>  7 x13    1949 Jul     NA
#>  8 x13    1949 Aug     NA
#>  9 x13    1949 Sep     NA
#> 10 x13    1949 Oct     NA
#> # ℹ 134 more rows
residuals(mb, type = "regression")    # linearized series
#> # A tsibble: 144 x 3 [1M]
#> # Key:       .model [1]
#>    .model    index .resid
#>    <chr>     <mth>  <dbl>
#>  1 x13    1949 Jan   4.71
#>  2 x13    1949 Feb   4.78
#>  3 x13    1949 Mar   4.90
#>  4 x13    1949 Apr   4.85
#>  5 x13    1949 May   4.79
#>  6 x13    1949 Jun   4.91
#>  7 x13    1949 Jul   4.99
#>  8 x13    1949 Aug   5.01
#>  9 x13    1949 Sep   4.92
#> 10 x13    1949 Oct   4.77
#> # ℹ 134 more rows
augment(mb)
#> # A tsibble: 144 x 6 [1M]
#> # Key:       .model [1]
#>    .model    index value .fitted .resid .innov
#>    <chr>     <mth> <dbl>   <dbl>  <dbl>  <dbl>
#>  1 x13    1949 Jan   112      NA     NA     NA
#>  2 x13    1949 Feb   118      NA     NA     NA
#>  3 x13    1949 Mar   132      NA     NA     NA
#>  4 x13    1949 Apr   129      NA     NA     NA
#>  5 x13    1949 May   121      NA     NA     NA
#>  6 x13    1949 Jun   135      NA     NA     NA
#>  7 x13    1949 Jul   148      NA     NA     NA
#>  8 x13    1949 Aug   148      NA     NA     NA
#>  9 x13    1949 Sep   136      NA     NA     NA
#> 10 x13    1949 Oct   119      NA     NA     NA
#> # ℹ 134 more rows
accuracy(mb)
#> # A tibble: 1 × 10
#>   .model .type         ME  RMSE   MAE     MPE  MAPE  MASE RMSSE   ACF1
#>   <chr>  <chr>      <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>   <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>  <dbl>
#> 1 x13    Training -0.0642  8.53  6.75 -0.0109  2.45 0.211 0.235 0.0200

# Interpolation of missing values
y_na <- y
y_na$value[c(20, 21)] <- NA
mb_na <- model(y_na, x13 = X13(value))
interpolate(mb_na, y_na)
#> # A tsibble: 144 x 2 [1M]
#>       index value
#>       <mth> <dbl>
#>  1 1949 Jan   112
#>  2 1949 Feb   118
#>  3 1949 Mar   132
#>  4 1949 Apr   129
#>  5 1949 May   121
#>  6 1949 Jun   135
#>  7 1949 Jul   148
#>  8 1949 Aug   148
#>  9 1949 Sep   136
#> 10 1949 Oct   119
#> # ℹ 134 more rows

# Updating a model when new observations arrive
start_new <- yearmonth("1960 Jan")
y_old  <- y[y$index < start_new, ]
y_new  <- y[y$index >= start_new, ]
mb_old <- model(y_old, x13 = X13(value))

# stream(): append the new observations, estimated parameters kept
mb_ext <- stream(mb_old, y_new)
components(mb_ext)
#> # A dable: 144 x 7 [1M]
#> # Key:     .model [1]
#> # :        value = trend * seasonal * irregular
#>    .model    index value trend seasonal irregular season_adjust
#>    <chr>     <mth> <dbl> <dbl>    <dbl>     <dbl>         <dbl>
#>  1 x13    1949 Jan   112  122.    0.919     0.995          122.
#>  2 x13    1949 Feb   118  125.    0.949     0.998          124.
#>  3 x13    1949 Mar   132  127.    1.05      0.997          126.
#>  4 x13    1949 Apr   129  128.    0.996     1.01           130.
#>  5 x13    1949 May   121  128.    0.943     1.00           128.
#>  6 x13    1949 Jun   135  127.    1.07      0.999          127.
#>  7 x13    1949 Jul   148  126.    1.19      0.989          125.
#>  8 x13    1949 Aug   148  126.    1.17      0.999          126.
#>  9 x13    1949 Sep   136  127.    1.07      1.00           128.
#> 10 x13    1949 Oct   119  128.    0.925     1.01           129.
#> # ℹ 134 more rows

# refit(): apply the model to the full data
refit(mb_old, y)                      # refresh policy "Fixed" (default)
#> # A mable: 1 x 1
#>                                x13
#>                            <model>
#> 1 <X-13ARIMA, ARIMA(0,1,1)(0,1,1)>
